title.narrative: Emergency Assistance for Reconstruction and Recovery of Marawi

description.narrative: The emergency assistance (ERRM) is structured to provide the GoP with immediate and flexible financing to implement programs, projects and activities included in the Bangon Marawi Comprehensive Rehabilitation and Recovery Program.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Adverse social impact of the armed conflict on affected persons mitigated

75% of Department of Education schools in Marawi and surrounding municipalities meeting Department of Education minimum standards for quality Achievement: 75 Progress/Status: At the request of the government, ADB facilitated the recruitment of implementation consultant firm (Save the Children Philippines or SCP) and 3 individual consultants. The contracts of SCP and 3 individual consultants have been extended until grant closing date of 31 December 2022. Construction of both the bagsakan facility and school building have been completed and turned over to the government.
The grant was financially closed in April 2024. Data Source: Department of Education records

24/7 potable water supply reestablished in 12 barangays (villages) (1,392 households; about 3,500 women) under the Marawi city water district Achievement: 12 Progress/Status: Originally, 19 barangays are to be covered but due to grant fund limitation, the scope of work was reduced to cover only 12 barangays. Based on data provided by MCWD, a total of 1,968 households will be served (5,807 male and 6,196 female) within the 12 barangays.
The grant was financially closed in September 2024. Data Source: Project construction records and project progress reports

At least 20% increase in people (50% women)b in Marawi and surrounding areas with improved access to health services Achievement: 300000 Progress/Status: All 4 consultants were mobilized in September 2019. The patient transport and monitoring vehicles and ambulances have been delivered to the recipient LGUs. DOH agreed to cancel the procurement of mobile health clinics, following several failures of bidding due to difficulty in sourcing out suppliers and likely shortage of funds arising from an expected increase in cost for the construction of health units and procurement of medical equipment. Contracts for goods have also been awarded as of 31 December 2021. The goods were already delivered to the health facilities. Construction of Marawi CHU and Lumbayanague RHU are already completed as of 30 June 2023. They are both now operational. As for consulting services, all consultants have been engaged with completion date of 30 June 2023. Two consultants are for extension until 30 September 2023 to assist in completing documentation for turnover and preparation of government's PCR.
The grant was financially closed in April 2024. Data Source: Clinic patient records

Remaining IDPs (disaggregated by sex) reduced by 80% (August 2018 baseline of remaining IDPs: 73,266 [54% female]) Achievement: 48577 Progress/Status: According to the report from the Task Force Bangon Marawi as of July 2022, 16,072 families (approximately 80,360 individuals) remain displaced from the May 2017 crisis in the city. Around 4,916 families (approximately 24,580 individuals) of which are still staying in various transitory sites, while the other 11,156 families (approximately 55,780 individuals) are in home-based setting. Permanent shelters in Marawi City and other parts of Lanao del Sur that accommodate a total of 1,621 families (8,105 individuals), on the other hand, were already set up as part of the government's rehabilitation program for the conflict-affected city. However, these families continue to face challenges that are similar to those who are situated in transitory sites particularly in achieving durable solutions. While the rehabilitation program of the government in Marawi, particularly in the most affected areas, is still on-going, 15 barangays belonging to Sectors 1 to 7 are now opened for the return of the displaced families. Families who are intending to return and reconstruct their houses need to undergo the Kathagombalay process to be accounted for and issued with necessary building permits. As of October 2022, there are 2,947 applicants for building permits but only 1,437 were approved. While displaced families are still struggling to get back to normalcy after the siege, the COVID-19 crisis exacerbated their situation.
Male/Female disaggregation: Not available.
(Source: UNHCR Mindanao Displacement Dashboard, November 2022- no updated info as of October 2023)
The loan was financially closed in December 2023. Data Source: TFBM progress reports on implementation of BMCRRP and status of IDPs

Output: Quick-disbursing support for the recovery program implemented Indicator: Up to 449 PPA in the BMCRRP implemented in the following categories: (i). local governance, (ii) housing assistance, (iii) business and livelihoods, and (iv) social services Achievement: 653 Progress/Status: As of 27 April 2020, L3768-PHI has been fully disbursed ($300 million). Output: Social services and livelihoods support improved Indicator: Conflict-sensitive education initiatives supported Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The project has engaged three youth engagement platforms namely, the Youth Leadership and Peace Summit, the Ranaw Youth Parliament and the Socially Excluded Youth. This covers the participation of youth in the executive and legislative arm in governance.
101 (Male -59, F, 42) youth participated in Youth Leadership Summit, female youth consisted of 42% of the total participants on this activity. The youth participants are from municipalities of Mulondo, Taraka Tamparan, Saguiaran, Butig, Lumba Bayabao, Pagayawan, Marantao, Marawi City and Maguing as part of efforts for Youth Peace Education for protection against recruitment to violent extremism in partnership with Armed Forces of the Philippines and UNDP.
52 (26 (50%) male, 26 (50%) female) youth participated in the Ranaw Youth Peace and Development training.
50 (20 (40%) male, 30 (60%) female) socially excluded youth participated in the Peacetival activities.
52 youth (23 male, 29 female) from municipalities of LDS participated in the 2nd Youth Leadership Summit conducted last July 26-30, 2021 in Marawi City, LDS supported by the project with focused areas on leadership skills formation and Peace Education. These youth will be engaged in the multi -stakeholder network for peace action.
Conflict sensitive and peacebuilding workshop conducted on May 24-26 to consolidate the peace action plan. A peacebuilding network strengthening was also conducted with the Education Workers Network of MBHTE to strengthen Peace Coalition with the Education Sector on June 20-22.
20 young leaders completed the Ranaw Young Leaders' Academy (RYLA) course. The module is finalized and will be the benchmark training course for young leaders for the province.
Data Source: Save the Children Philippines quarterly monitoring report and DepED BARMM EMIS Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
